corrections.claim: batman exposure integration for Kepler long cadence: exp_time = 1765.464 s / 86400 d
corrections.correction: 1765.46 s is the Kepler long-cadence *interval* (TIMEDEL = 0.0204336 d), not the integration time. The Q10 TPF header of kplr005689116 (downloaded in the sandbox) gives INT_TIME 6.0198 s, READTIME 0.5189 s, NUM_FRM 270, so the photons are integrated for 270 x 6.0198 = 1625.35 s (92% of the cadence). Use exp_time = 1625.35/86400 (the brief's value over-smears the model by ~8%; the fitted parameters quoted in the brief were produced with the larger value and should be re-run). For TESS 30-min FFIs the TESScut S14 header gives EXPOSURE 0.0165 d = 1425.6 s against TIMEDEL 1800 s (cosmic-ray mitigation removes 20%); 10-min and 200-s FFIs scale the same way, so always read EXPOSURE/INT_TIME x NUM_FRM from the product header rather than assuming the cadence.
corrections.evidence: lightkurve download of 'KIC 5689116' Q10 TPF, hdu[1].header: INT_TIME 6.01980290327, READTIME 0.518948526144, NUM_FRM 270, TIMEDEL 0.02043359821692, FRAMETIM 6.5388; TESScut tess-s0014-2-3 cutout header: EXPOSURE 0.016499992 d, TIMEDEL 0.0208333 d, NUM_FRM 900, INT_TIME 1.98 s

corrections.claim: use_threads defaults to all cores — set it explicitly in a multiprocessing pipeline
corrections.correction: Confirmed and sharpened by test: TLS 2.0.1 with use_threads=2 inside a multiprocessing.Pool worker raises AssertionError('daemonic processes are not allowed to have children') because TLS spawns its own persistent worker-process pool; use_threads=1 works inside Pool, and use_threads>1 works inside concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor (non-daemonic workers). TLS keeps its pool alive between power() calls (WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT 300 s) and relies on 'fork' (15 ms start) — 'spawn'/'forkserver' (Linux from Python 3.14) costs ~3 s per pool start.

corrections.claim: Jenkins 2002, ApJ 575, 493 (wavelet matched filter) — from memory
corrections.correction: Secondary sources (Kepler pipeline overview arXiv:1001.0258) confirm the Kepler TPS uses 'the wavelet-based adaptive matched filter from Jenkins (2002)' and a 7.1 sigma folded-statistic (MES) threshold; the ApJ page itself was not fetched.

additions: Exposure-time correctness: Kepler LC integration is 1625.35 s (INT_TIME 6.0198 s x NUM_FRM 270) inside a 1765.46 s cadence; TESS 30-min FFI integration is 1425.6 s inside 1800 s (10-min: 475.2 s in 600 s; 200-s: 158.4 s in 200 s by the same 0.8 factor — read EXPOSURE from the header). Using the cadence as exp_time over-smears the model; using none biases rho_star low (Kipping 2010). KBONUS per-quarter headers carry no EXPOSURE/TIMEDEL, so take them from the originating TPF.

TLS 2 inside a worker pool: use_threads>1 fails inside multiprocessing.Pool workers (daemonic) with AssertionError; works in ProcessPoolExecutor or with use_threads=1. TLS keeps a persistent fork-based pool alive 300 s between power() calls, so a long-lived worker that calls TLS repeatedly amortises the ~15 ms pool start; the first call per process compiles numba kernels (seconds) — set NUMBA_CACHE_DIR to a writable per-user path so workers share the cache.

Time systems, explicit: KBONUS TIME is BKJD = BJD_TDB - 2454833 (TPF header BJDREFI 2454833, TIMESYS TDB); TESS products use BTJD = BJD_TDB - 2457000 (BJDREFI 2457000); hence Kuber's -2167 d. Kuber's T0 = BJD 2455630.245431 = BKJD 797.245431 = BTJD -1369.754569. Mixing them by one day shifts a 13.77-d ephemeris by 0.07 in phase and destroys any TESS stack.

Kepler data-gap anatomy measured on this star: quarter boundaries 0.9-4.8 d, Q7->Q8 15.8 d (safe mode), and three missing quarters (Q5, Q9, Q13: Module 3 failure, the originating TPF's channel) producing 92-105 d gaps; 57 intra-quarter gaps > 0.5 d. Period searches should treat the 93-d quarter cycle and the 372.5-d Kepler orbit (and their harmonics) and periods commensurate with the 29.424-min cadence as suspect systematics, the Kepler analogue of the 13.7-d TESS pile-up. Kepler rolling-band artefacts are flagged by bits 131072/262144, which are NOT in lightkurve's default bitmask.

SNR statistics are not interchangeable: astropy BLS 'snr' = depth/depth_err (local, ignores trials and red noise), TLS SNR = depth/std x sqrt(N_in-transit), LEO/Kepler MES is the matched-filter multiple-event statistic (Kepler used MES >= 7.1, Jenkins 2002 wavelet whitening; Robovetter metrics in Thompson et al. 2018). eumemic's calibration shows MES < 10 signals are ~46% noise even at BLS SNR >= 9. Report all three for a candidate and never compare a BLS-SNR threshold to a MES threshold.

BLS box depth is biased low versus the physical depth for limb-darkened, cadence-smeared transits (this star: BLS box 1649 ppm vs TLS 1999 ppm vs batman (rp/rs)^2 1959 ppm vs Kuber 2165-2348 ppm PSF). Quote the model-fit depth; use box depths only for consistency tests (odd/even, per-quarter, holdout).

Alias discipline: restricting the TLS/BLS period range to 1-10 d found P/2 = 6.885 d of a 13.77-d signal (run B). After any detection test P/2, 2P, 3P/2, 2P/3 explicitly (eumemic known_alias uses the 1/3..3 harmonic set) and require the odd/even and 'depth_half' statistics to agree before trusting the period.

Grid sanity for astropy BLS: durations must be strictly shorter than the minimum trial period (astropy raises otherwise), and `dy` must be the empirical per-segment scatter — the 'snr' objective scales with dy while the median-normalised SDE does not; use oversample >= 5 at the refine stage (eumemic uses 10) so the box centre is not quantised coarser than the 30-min cadence.

Separate-venv list (now evidence-based): TRICERATOPS (pytransit==2.2, setuptools<81), psfmachine (numpy<2, pandas<2, astropy<6, Python <= 3.11 in practice), tglc (wotan~=1.9, numpy<2, python<3.13), MonoTools (lightkurve==1.11.0, scipy==1.12), SHERLOCK (docs: Python 3.10; PyPI metadata: >=3.11). Installing any of them into the search venv silently downgrades wotan/numpy and changes search results.

LEO-Vetter practicalities: TCELightCurve(tic, time, raw, flux, flux_err, per, epo, dur) wants `dur` in days and times in the same system as `epo`; `compute_flux_metrics(star)` needs star['rad','e_rad','mass','e_mass','Teff','e_Teff','rho','u1','u2','id','planetData'] (KeyError 'e_rad' is the first failure if omitted, as the previous agent hit); pixel_vetting needs the external transitDiffImage package and TESS sector/cam/ccd, so for Kepler the pixel stage must be home-made (Kuber's pixel_localize.py pattern).

Provenance for reproducibility: record git SHA of the pipeline, `uv pip freeze` with hashes, numba/TLS versions, random seeds (emcee, scrambles), the frozen target CSV with its SHA-256, and the pre-registered holdout split per star (Kuber writes <id>_split.json before searching). TLS 2 changed results in 10 bug fixes, so a result produced with TLS 1.x (as Kuber's Python 3.10 environment did) is not bit-reproducible with TLS 2.0.1.

Second-aperture / second-reduction checks are tooling-cheap and should be standard: KBONUS gives FLUX (PSF), PSF_FLAT_FLUX and SAP_FLUX in the same file; Chopra compared SPOC vs QLP; eumemic prefers SPOC > TESS-SPOC > QLP. A transit that survives in only one reduction is a red flag; one that appears in SAP with depth tracking the flux fraction (Kuber's dilution test) supports the target as host.

Rotation handling before the blind search: eumemic prewhitens (Lomb-Scargle 0.1-10 d on 30-min bins, 4 harmonics, chunked) only when P_rot < 3 d and variability SNR > 3; for everything else a 0.5-1.0 d biweight suffices. Masked GP (celerite2) is for fitting, not for the blind search (wotan 2.0 'gp' took 55 s on 4,400 points).
remaining_uncertainties: The batman+emcee result in Section 6.1 was produced with exp_time = 1765.464 s (the Kepler cadence); re-running with the integration time 1625.35 s will shift a/Rs, b and rho_star slightly (the direction: less smearing -> slightly sharper ingress -> higher rho_star), so the quoted 5.9 rho_sun is provisional.

TLS 2's BUGLOG.md could not be fetched (404 at raw main/master; GitHub API blocked from this sandbox), so the exact list of the 10 result-changing fixes and any re-calibrated SDE-vs-FAP table for TLS 2 on red-noise Kepler/TESS data remain unknown; the FAQ table is still the TLS 1.x white-noise one.
All wall-clock costs (BLS 150-440 s, TLS 100-200 s per Kepler star) were measured while other agents loaded the 4 vCPUs; re-measure on an idle box before sizing a cloud run.

eumemic's semi-coherent/stack-slide BLS misses ~15% of weak signals the coherent search finds; the right trade-off for 13-quarter Kepler light curves cut into 90-d blocks has not been measured by injection-recovery.
